ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: conntrack usage at 98% on us-west2-gpu-prod nodes (fleet-*/gpu-*) — packet drops / TCP resets observed, pods reporting connection errors. Please triage.

sam: seeing a heap of failed inference GRPC streams, retries spiking. Jobs 8472/8476 failing intermittently.

lina: confirmed on a handful of nodes: `conntrack -S` shows ~430k entries, nf_conntrack_max=524288. spikes correlate with pods doing many short-lived outbound connections (healthchecks + model pulls).

matt: FYI we're using Calico overlay + iptables masquerade for pod egress; that creates conntrack entries for many ephemeral src/dst tuples. Also NAT gateway NATing for cross-az egress might be contributing.

olivia: quick triage steps I ran: `kubectl top nodes` shows CPU fine, but `ss -s` shows high TCP memory/estab resets. Attached small dump: ```
# conntrack -L | tail -n 8
tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.10.2.34 dst=10.10.7.12 sport=42000 dport=54321 packets=3 bytes=192
tcp      6 120 SYN_SENT src=10.10.5.67 dst=3.218.11.45 sport=50234 dport=443 ...
```

sam: options: 1) increase nf_conntrack_max on nodes (short term) 2) reduce conntrack footprints (disable SNAT for cluster CIDR / use iptables NO-MASQUERADE) 3) switch calico to eBPF mode to reduce kernel NAT churn. Thoughts?

lina: agree. quick mitigation: bump nf_conntrack_max to 1M and lower tcp timeout for time_wait/established where safe. commands I used: ```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1000000
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
``` Note: these don't persist across reboots — will push via node sysctl DaemonSet config.

matt: be careful — simply increasing max masks the underlying cause. We should also remove unnecessary SNAT for cluster-internal traffic: set --cluster-cidr in kube-proxy and enable "masqueradeAll=false" or use ipvs with proper skip-snat CIDR. For our setup, edit kube-proxy ConfigMap: ```kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap kube-proxy
# set 'mode: ipvs' and 'conntrack:
#   maxPerCore: 32768
#   tcpEstablishedTimeout: 86400'
```

olivia: adding datapoint: observed a stampede pattern — many pods create short HTTPS connections to external model-hosting buckets (per-request auth). That explodes conntrack. We should gate that with connection pooling / shared cache service to reduce flows. Product flagged as well.

sam: short-term plan agreed:
- Lina to roll a DaemonSet that sets nf_conntrack_max=1M and reduces timeouts (apply to all us-west2 gpu nodes) — ETA 30m
- Matt to patch kube-proxy config for ipvs + adjust conntrack per-core and disable unnecessary masquerade for cluster CIDR — ETA 2h
- Olivia to open a ticket with infra-devs to add connection pooling in the inference sidecar for model-host fetches — tracking #INF-289
- Ops-bot will monitor conntrack usage and page if >90% after changes.

lina: starting DaemonSet now — will apply sysctl via privileged init and then roll nodes (cordon/uncordon minimal). posting pod logs: ```
I0321 15:02:11.123 DaemonSet sysctl-applier starting on node gpu-12
applied net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1000000
applied net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300
```

matt: while Lina rolls, I'm drafting the kube-proxy patch. We'll use a 30% staged rollout to avoid mass iptables churn. Also adding conntrack helpers to kubelet kubeproxy flags.

deploy-bot: Finished: kube-proxy configmap patch v2 queued for canary on us-west2-a (3 nodes).

sam: early checks — conntrack counts dropping on canary nodes, error rate down ~70% for failing jobs. Nice. :thumbsup:

olivia: I'll coordinate with devs for the pooling change, but short-term increase + kube-proxy changes should buy time. Also scheduling a follow-up postmortem to look at traffic patterns and cross-az NAT behavior.

lina: leaving notes in infra runbook: "conntrack saturation — signs, quick sysctl DaemonSet, kube-proxy ipvs patch, long-term: reduce SNAT, eBPF calico."

sam: action items captured. closing thread when monitoring stable. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
